edge.rationale: Tenths are the first decimal fractional unit in decimal place-value work.
Hundredths are a core decimal place-value unit and bridge to percent.
Thousandths extend decimal place-value structure beyond hundredths.
The decimal point structures decimal place-value interpretation.
Number lines support decimal magnitude and location.
Comparing and ordering decimals directly practises decimal place value.
Rounding decimals applies place-value and magnitude reasoning.
Decimal place value is grounded in fractions with powers-of-ten denominators.
Decimal addition and subtraction are central decimal operations.
Multiplying decimals by whole numbers extends whole-number multiplication and decimal place value.
Dividing decimals by whole numbers extends sharing and decimal place value.
Percent as hundredths is the core meaning of percent notation.
Percent concepts require moving among fraction, decimal and percent representations.
Benchmark percentages support estimation and flexible percent reasoning.
Finding percent of a quantity is a core application of percent concepts.
Percentage increase and decrease directly practise percentage change.
Tenths as decimals build on interpreting tenths as fractional units.
edge.failure_signal: Learner writes decimals without relating them to one-tenth units.

edge.rationale: Hundredths extend the tenths place by subdividing tenths into ten equal parts.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot explain why 0.10 equals one tenth or ten hundredths.

edge.rationale: Thousandths extend the decimal place-value sequence beyond hundredths.
edge.failure_signal: Learner treats thousandths as larger than hundredths because 1000 is larger than 100.

edge.rationale: Decimal-point interpretation depends on understanding places to the right of ones.
edge.failure_signal: Learner reads 3.45 as two unrelated whole numbers 3 and 45.

edge.rationale: Locating decimals on number lines requires interpreting decimal notation as magnitude.
edge.failure_signal: Learner places 0.7 after 0.65 based on digit length rather than magnitude.

edge.rationale: Number-line magnitude supports comparing and ordering decimal values.
edge.failure_signal: Learner thinks 0.62 is greater than 0.7 because 62 is greater than 7.

edge.rationale: Rounding decimals depends on comparing a value to nearby benchmark decimal values.
edge.failure_signal: Learner rounds by changing digits without considering place or magnitude.

edge.rationale: Decimal-fraction equivalence uses tenths and hundredths as powers-of-ten fractional units.
Adding and subtracting decimals requires aligning like decimal place values.
edge.failure_signal: Learner aligns the last digits rather than the decimal points or place values.

edge.rationale: Multiplying decimals by whole numbers extends multiplication facts and place-value scaling.
edge.failure_signal: Learner calculates digits but cannot estimate the product magnitude.

edge.rationale: Dividing decimals by whole numbers extends equal sharing to decimal quantities.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot interpret 1.2 divided by 3 as sharing a decimal quantity.

edge.rationale: Percent as per hundred depends on interpreting hundredths.
Fraction-decimal-percent equivalence builds on decimal and fraction equivalence for hundredths.
edge.failure_signal: Learner treats 0.5, 1/2 and 50% as unrelated quantities.

edge.rationale: Benchmark percentages require interpreting common percents as parts per hundred.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot use 50% as half or 25% as one quarter.

edge.rationale: Finding percent of a quantity builds from benchmark percent reasoning to more general cases.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot identify the base quantity or estimate a reasonable percent amount.

edge.rationale: Percentage increase and decrease require finding a percent of the original amount and applying it as a change.
edge.failure_signal: Learner changes by the percent number itself rather than by the percent of the base amount.
